title: Building Blocks of STEM Act
official_summary:
Building Blocks of STEM Act

This bill modifies National Science Foundation (NSF) grant programs that support STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, including computer science) education.

(Sec. 3) The bill instructs the NSF, when awarding grants under the Discovery Research PreK-12 program, to improve the focus of research and development on elementary and prekindergarten education.

(Sec. 4) The bill specifies that NSF grants to increase the participation of underrepresented populations in STEM fields may be used for research into various subjects regarding female students in prekindergarten through elementary school, including

  • the role of teachers and caregivers in encouraging or discouraging participation by such students in STEM activities, and
  • the types of STEM activities that encourage greater participation by such students.

(Sec. 5) The bill specifies that NSF grants to research computer science education and computational thinking may be used to support development and implementation of various tools and models for teaching and learning, including

  • developing and offering female-inclusive computer science enrichment programs, and
  • acquainting female students in prekindergarten through elementary school with careers in computer science.

summary.headline: This law directs the National Science Foundation to focus some of its STEM education grants on early childhood and elementary learning, including research on girls' participation in STEM.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes how the National Science Foundation awards certain STEM education grants. It tells the agency to focus its Discovery Research PreK-12 grants more on prekindergarten and elementary education. It also allows grants aimed at increasing participation by underrepresented groups to fund research on female students in prekindergarten through elementary school, including the role of teachers and caregivers. Finally, it allows computer science education grants to support tools, programs, and career exposure for these young female students.

who_it_affects.group: Young girls in prekindergarten through elementary school
who_it_affects.how: Federal grants may now be used to fund STEM and computer science enrichment programs and career exposure aimed at them.

who_it_affects.group: Teachers and caregivers of young children
who_it_affects.how: The law allows federal research into how their roles encourage or discourage young girls' participation in STEM activities.

who_it_affects.group: Researchers and educational institutions that apply for National Science Foundation grants
who_it_affects.how: Applicants for these grant programs may now propose projects focused on early elementary education and young female students.
